summary: FirstEnergy Service Company asks for rehearing of FERC's September 29, 2026 order that accepted PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement subject to a three-topic paper hearing. It challenges four findings on price structure, resource eligibility, supplier performance and demand response gating.
ask: Grant rehearing and reject the levelized price framework (or require straight-line pricing or an annual cap), require priority for firm dispatchable capacity, strengthen supplier performance assurance, and require binding commitments for demand response.

points.point: FirstEnergy says the September 29 order accepts the RBP except three paper-hearing topics but does not answer its arguments on the rest.
points.quote: the September 29 Order accepts the filing, declares that every aspect of the RBP other than three discrete topics set for paper hearing is just and reasonable

points.point: FirstEnergy says the order suspended the RBP five months to February 28, 2027 and set a paper hearing on cost allocation, TO exit rules and LSE collateral.
points.quote: suspended them for five months to become effective February 28, 2027, subject to refund

points.point: FERC granted PJM's abeyance request, moving initial briefs to January 11, 2027 and reply briefs to January 26, 2027.
points.quote: extending the deadline for initial briefs in the paper hearing Docket No. EL26-108-000 from November 13, 2026 to January 11, 2027

points.point: The $555/MW-day cap is a levelized average, which FirstEnergy says lets sellers front-load prices into early years.
points.quote: sellers will front-load their costs into the initial years of their contracts.

points.point: It asks FERC to require firm, dispatchable resources to be prioritized, citing NERC reliability evidence.
points.quote: The Commission should grant rehearing and require PJM to demonstrate that the RBP framework appropriately prioritizes firm and dependable capacity resources.

points.point: Shortfall charges apply only before commercial operation, so customers lack protection against underperformance over the 15-year term.
LSEs post $1.5 million per RBP MW in collateral while sellers post only three years of shortfall charges.
points.quote: Customers are asked to post collateral of $1.5 million per committed RBP MW to protect suppliers for up to fifteen years

points.point: It asks FERC to clarify that demand response must be backed by binding contractual commitments, not just a plan.
points.quote: clarify that Demand Resources and DER Capacity Aggregation Resources must be supported by binding contractual commitments to provide the
